description: Easily create full virtual machines that are sandboxed for development or computer use models.

latest_release.name: Release 0.1.14 -  Crushing some bugs
latest_release.body:
### New

- Running out of space in a VM? Shut it down, open **Edit**, and increase **Disk Size**. The system volume expands automatically on the next boot. You can also grow the disk through the API or MCP. Disk increases are permanent in App Sandbox. Thanks to @ayangg294 and @MattSpark27 for requesting this, @urlocalguru for sharing a workaround, @lhjofre for flagging the missing edit option, and @mvscottdev, @nithinp1, @phant0mon, and @zDropedZXZ for supporting the request. ([#89](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/89), [#12 comment](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/12#issuecomment-4640698885), [#57 comment](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/57#issuecomment-4691212735))

  For older VMs, see Compatibility at the bottom of this post for upgrade instructions.

- Select an existing external Hyper-V switch when creating or editing a VM on Windows. VMs can share a switch with the host, WSL, or other VMs. The selection is available in the GUI, API, and MCP. Thanks to @Poldino95 and @Loyola-London for reporting the adapter conflict, @xjasonli for proposing switch reuse, and @caulmseh for reporting the missing adapter selector when editing a VM. ([#231](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/231), [#157](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/pull/157), [#240](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/240#issuecomment-7070879767))

### Fixed

- Show the virtual disk’s actual capacity, including after a disk was expanded outside App Sandbox. Thanks to @danbrakeley for reporting the stale size. ([#113](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/113))
- Preserve HCS guest and runtime state across cold starts on Windows hosts, including the virtual TPM state used by Windows Hello. Thanks to @hitem for reporting a cold-start failure after rolling back a Windows update and @Poldino95 for identifying the Windows Hello PIN reset. ([#162](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/pull/162), [comment](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/pull/162#issuecomment-6992587955))
- Stop attaching installer ISOs to VMs on Windows hosts. Installed VMs can start after the original ISO is moved or deleted. Thanks to @Stormrider80 for reporting the startup failure, @miyatsu for reporting slow restarts, and @Muguett-DBY for tracing the missing ISO error. ([#237](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/discussions/237), [#81](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/81), [comment](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/discussions/237#discussioncomment-19775304))
- If the selected External adapter or switch is unavailable at startup, clear the selection and start the VM without a virtual network adapter. Thanks to @kurokawaikki for reporting that unavailable External networking blocked startup. ([#92](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/issues/92))

### Compatibility

- **VMs created with an earlier App Sandbox release need a guest agent update inside the VM before you can grow their disks.** For Windows and macOS guests, follow the [VM upgrade guide](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/blob/main/VM-UPGRADE.md).
- Disk growth supports fully installed, stopped Windows and Ubuntu guests on Windows hosts, and Windows and macOS guests on macOS hosts. On Windows hosts, the VM must be free of snapshots and branches.
- The Windows-host startup and networking changes work with existing Windows and Ubuntu guest components.

### Think App Sandbox is useful?

If you use it for something interesting or helpful, it would be really helpful if you could mention it online somewhere!

detail.readme: # App Sandbox App Sandbox is a virtual machine app for Windows and macOS that's focused on performance and ease of use. [![All-time downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/total?style=for-the-badge&label=All-time%20downloads)](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/releases) Windows features: - Works on Windows 11 Home or Pro, without Hyper-V - Windows 11 or Ubuntu 26.04 LTS VM Support - Zero touch install - Copy and Paste - 2 Channel Audio - GPU Acceleration via Paravirtualization (GPU-PV) with support for DirectX 12, 11, 10, 9 (Windows only), OpenGL, Vulkan, CUDA, OpenCL - When an NVIDIA GPU is shared, DLSS and CUDA is supported - GPU Hardware Video Decoder/Encoder support - SSH via Hyper-V socket proxy (no network required) - Snapshots - Multiple resolution options as well as optional dynamic resolution, and fullscreen mode - Host to client hot-key support - Provision and boot with / without internet - Supports running Claude Cowork and Docker inside the VM thanks to Nested Virtualization Support - Local API, MCP server, and Python SDK Mac features: - macOS or Windows 11 ARM VM support - Zero touch install - Copy and Paste - 2 Channel Audio - macOS: GPU Acceleration via Paravirtualization with support for Metal, Windows: No GPU Acceleration - SSH via virtio-vsock (no network required) - Dynamic display sizing (optional on Windows) and fullscreen mode - Provision and boot with / without internet - Local API, MCP server, and Python SDK Requirements: Windows 11 with an x64 Processor or macOS 27 or newer (M Series) ## About App Sandbox App Sandbox creates and runs full desktop virtual machines — Windows 11, Ubuntu, and macOS. It is free and open-source (MIT), distributed as prebuilt binaries (EV-signed on Windows, Apple-Developer-signed on macOS) on its [Releases](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/releases) page. Use the graphical UI or automate it through the API, MCP server, or Python SDK. Pick an OS and an installer image, and App Sandbox provisions the disk, runs an unattended install, and boots the guest. You supply a Windows or Ubuntu ISO; macOS guests download their restore image automatically. It runs on a Windows 11 (x64) PC or an Apple Silicon Mac, including laptops. **Runs on Windows 11 Home, without Hyper-V.** On Windows, App Sandbox does not use Hyper-V or Hyper-V Manager; it creates and runs VMs through the Windows Host Compute System (HCS) and Host Compute Network (HCN) APIs, which require only the *Virtual Machine Platform* feature. Hyper-V is limited to Windows 11 Pro and Enterprise, while Virtual Machine Platform is available on Windows 11 Home, so a Windows 11 Pro license is not required. Virtual Machine Platform is the same Windows feature WSL2 uses. **What you can use it for:** - A full Windows or Ubuntu **desktop** VM — a complete graphical OS with GPU acceleration (OpenGL, Vulkan, CUDA, DLSS, D3D) — for building and testing your own software on a clean install. - Running a program in a VM, kept separate from your main OS and files. - Developing and testing Windows drivers: a built-in **Test Mode** enables test-signing inside the guest, so the host's Secure Boot and boot configuration are left unchanged. - Running a computer-use AI agent (such as Claude's computer use model) in its own VM. App Sandbox provides the desktop and the VM; the agent's own model loop runs inside the guest. Several agents can run at once, each in its own VM, on a single laptop or desktop. - Creating GPU-accelerated (**GPU-PV**) VMs, from the GUI or the headless API. - Scripting the VM lifecycle from code — create, snapshot, branch, SSH into, and delete GPU-accelerated VMs — with the Python SDK. **API and MCP.** App Sandbox supports automation through a local HTTP API, MCP server, and Python SDK on Windows and macOS, with the GUI or in headless mode. See the [API, MCP, and Python SDK documentation](tools/headless-api/README.md) for setup and usage. **How it works:** this repo also aims to be a working example of creating full desktop VMs programmatically with the Windows HCS/HCN APIs and Apple's Virtualization.framework. On Windows, App Sandbox submits a hand-built HCS machine document to `computecore.dll` / `computenetwork.dll` — the HCS/HCN layer that also underlies WSL2 and Windows Sandbox — rather than going through Hyper-V Manager. GPU acceleration uses GPU paravirtualization (GPU-PV) to share the host's installed GPU with the guest — the same WSL2 path, not a dedicated passthrough (no VFIO/IOMMU, no second GPU). Windows guests get DirectX 12, 11, 10, 9, OpenGL, Vulkan, CUDA, and OpenCL; Ubuntu guests the same minus DirectX; macOS guests Metal. A custom **IddCx** indirect display driver and a virtual audio device carry the screen and sound, and guest↔host clipboard, audio, input, and SSH run over **Hyper-V sockets**. Guest disks are built by an in-repo tool with support for ext4, squashfs, qcow2, and VHDX. On macOS, App Sandbox uses Apple's **Virtualization.framework** (`VZVirtualMachine`, `VZMacOSInstaller`) over **virtio-vsock**. On Windows, Linux (Ubuntu) guests reach the GPU through a custom DRM/KMS kernel module (`asb_drm`), Microsoft's WSL2 `dxgkrnl`, and a custom Mesa build. The apps are native C / Objective-C with an HTML/JS UI (WebView2 on Windows, WKWebView on macOS). Windows guests on macOS use **QEMU 11.1.3** with HVF acceleration, built from our public [asb-qemu fork](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/asb-qemu/tree/asb-ivshmem-11.1.3). It preserves our four ivshmem changes, including support on macOS and the optional `x-device-id` override. QEMU, its libraries, and firmware ship inside the macOS app. See the [QEMU build notes](vendor/qemu-ivshmem/README.md) for the pinned source and rebuild instructions. # Tips: The default username is `user` and the default password is `test123` Want to give your old VM the new App Sandbox features? Download and run the new App Sandbox version and give your AI agent this [prompt](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/blob/main/VM-UPGRADE.md) to help with the upgrade [Windows] Enter fullscreen mode my right clicking the title bar and selecting borderless fullscreen mode. To exit this mode hold your mouse up on the top of the screen for about 1 second, then you'll see an option to exit. When your VM is running and open, right clicking its title bar will show several options like transmit hotkeys, mute audio and match window size where your VM display dynamically resizes to your viewers size. [Windows] Need a high performance remote desktop to remotely access your VM? [Phaze](https://phaze.app) works well [Windows] You can check if the GPU-PV driver setup is working by running gpu-test.exe inside your App Sandbox Windows VM, gpu-test.exe will show a box with 6 rotating cubes, each using a different rendering engine (D3D9, D3D10, D3D11, D3D12, OpenGL and Vulkan). If one or more fail, they will not correctly show a rotating cube for that rendering API. [gpu-test.zip](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/appsandbox/releases/download/v0.1.2/gpu-test.zip). Note: The rendering API succeeding means that the GPU-PV worked, but sometimes games or apps are coded in such a way that they will not detect the GPU-PV system correctly and still show an error. ## How to support the project Show people on Reddit, Twitter, Youtube, Tiktok or your favorite forum how you use App Sandbox to do something cool. Even if you just mention it's one of the tools in your workflow that would be super helpful, and will bring a lot of awareness to the project! ## Sharing fixes and features Thank you for sharing fixes and ideas! Pull requests, including AI-assisted changes from your own fork, are welcome as suggestions. They are unlikely to be formally reviewed or merged, but contributions that help shape a change will be credited. See the [contribution guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. ## License AppSandbox is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE) — Copyright (c) 2026 James Stringer. Guest drivers and bundled third-party components retain their own licenses, including [asb-dxgkrnl](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/asb-dxgkrnl), [asb-mesa](https://github.com/jamesstringer90/asb-mesa), and QEMU. AppSandbox's Linux DRM module (`tools/linux/asb_drm/`) is dual-licensed MIT OR GPL-2.0. See [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) for component licenses and source links. ## Acknowledgements Beyond my own experience building [Easy-GPU-PV](https://github.com/jamesstringerparsec/Easy-GPU-PV), I found [NanaBox](https://github.com/M2Team/NanaBox) to be a really helpful resource for understanding HCS. ## Author [James Stringer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesstringerphotography/) — author of [Easy-GPU-PV](https://github.com/jamesstringerparsec/Easy-GPU-PV).
